record.context_brief: Uniqueness of ultrapower embeddings up to unitary conjugacy
record.original_question: Is there a nonamenable separable II_1 factor N such that every pair of embeddings of N into its ultrapower N^U are conjugate by a unitary in N^U?

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Is there a non amenable separable II1 factor N such that any pair of embeddings of N into NU are conjugate by a unitary in NU?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable II$_1$ factor with separable predual, normalized faithful trace $\tau_N$, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. The tracial ultrapower $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ is the II$_1$ factor obtained as the quotient of $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N},N)$ by the two-sided ideal of sequences $(x_n)$ with $\lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}} \tau_N(x_n^* x_n)=0$, equipped with the trace $\tau((x_n)) = \lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}} \tau_N(x_n)$. By an embedding of $N$ into $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ we mean a unital, trace-preserving $*$-homomorphism $\pi: N \hookrightarrow N^{\mathcal{U}}$. Two such embeddings $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are said to be unitarily conjugate in $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ if there exists a unitary $u \in N^{\mathcal{U}}$ with $\pi_2(x) = u\pi_1(x)u^*$ for every $x \in N$.

Recall that $N$ is amenable (equivalently, hyperfinite, isomorphic to the unique separable hyperfinite II$_1$ factor $\mathcal{R}$) if it admits an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional $*$-subalgebras with weakly dense union. Otherwise $N$ is called nonamenable.

Question: Does there exist a nonamenable separable II$_1$ factor $N$ such that for every free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, any two embeddings of $N$ into $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ are unitarily conjugate in $N^{\mathcal{U}}$?
artifact.status_search_result: A theorem of Jung (extended by Atkinson–Goldbring–Kunnawalkam Elayavalli) states that among Connes-embeddable separable II$_1$ factors, only the hyperfinite factor $\mathcal R$ has the property that all embeddings into its ultrapower are unitarily conjugate. Whether some non-Connes-embeddable (hence nonamenable) separable II$_1$ factor enjoys this "Jung property" is recognized as an open problem; recent work of Atkinson–Goldbring on the generalized Jung property and on non-embeddable factors resembling $\mathcal R$ explicitly leaves this question unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Factorial relative commutants and the generalized Jung property for II_1 factors
status_evidence.snippet: Among R^U-embeddable II_1 factors, R is the unique generalized Jung factor; existence of non-R^U-embeddable Jung factors is left open.
status_evidence.claim: Within the Connes-embeddable class, R is the unique factor with the unitary-conjugacy property; the nonamenable (necessarily non-Connes-embeddable) case is open.

status_evidence.title: Non-embeddable II_1 factors resembling the hyperfinite II_1 factor (Jung-Enforceable)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs non-Connes-embeddable factors with various R-like properties, but the unitary-conjugacy Jung property in this setting remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions produce nonamenable factors approximating Jung-type properties, but uniqueness of embeddings up to unitary conjugacy in N^U is not established.
